extracted.intended_audience: writers and creative-writers seeking prompts and practical guidance for micro fiction (very short stories)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and prompts for crafting micro fiction — complete short stories told in 300 words or fewer, with practical structure advice and tips for economy of language. Includes 100 prompts to spark micro-story ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count constraint (micro fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Micro fiction—short stories that dance within the constraint of 300 words or fewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the entire story to 300 words or fewer; this constraint defines micro fiction as distinct from longer flash fiction (noted as 300–1,500 words elsewhere on the site).

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity and precision (every word counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Micro fiction is an exercise in brevity and precision. It thrives on conveying a complete story with a beginning, middle, and end within the confines of a few hundred words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim unnecessary detail; choose language that carries maximal meaning and implication. Treat each word as contributing to character, plot, or emotional effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete narrative arc despite brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey a beginning, middle, and end even within a very small word count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to introduce the main character and initial situation (beginning), present the pivotal event (middle), and show aftermath or transformation (end) — all within the micro-fiction constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural proportions (beginning/middle/end)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested micro-fiction structure: beginning ≈ 25% of total words; middle ≈ 60%; end ≈ 15%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginning: introduce main character and initial state. Middle: present the main event/core moment that propels the narrative. End: briefly show the aftermath and how the character is changed, leaving closure or contemplation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start close to the end (narrative placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin your story as close to the main event as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starting near the pivotal moment maximizes impact and reduces wasted setup in limited space — immerse readers immediately in the heart of the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on the main event (centralize the story)
rubrics_metrics.description: Center the narrative around the pivotal event; trim extraneous details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the single key moment that drives the story and prioritize scenes, images, and lines that support it. Avoid side plots, long backstory, or irrelevant description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exit quickly with resonance (concise ending)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Get out’ quickly: wrap up the story in as few words as possible while still giving a sense of closure, contemplation, and/or emotional resonance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endings should be short but meaningful — suggest transformation or consequence rather than exhaustively explaining everything. Aim for an evocative final line or image that lingers.
